reportsWithoutComparing: row level security per table (the migration chain does not declare it, so there is nothing to expect)

whether a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE the chain asks for is actually present: the name PostgreSQL would give it is accepted when the live database has it, and its absence is not reported, so a hosted database that lost a unique index reads as a match on that point
notCompared: constraint definitions (PostgreSQL reformats them, so a textual diff would be noise)
the columns behind an index PostgreSQL built itself for a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE: the name the server would give it is recognised, the key columns behind it are not re-derived
row contents (this tool reads structure only)
grants, storage, tablespaces and extension membership

snapshot: Before any migration is approved against this database, the founder takes a recoverable Neon snapshot (or a pg_dump of the same branch) and records its id. Then apply, then re-run this tool and compare the two reports. A matching report from this tool is a precondition for a migration, never a substitute for the snapshot.
reading: matches false is the answer to "can the chain be applied as-is?", not a crash. This file authorises nothing: the founder takes a recoverable snapshot, then the founder applies, then this tool is re-run and the two reports compared.
